steps.text: Place eggs into a saucepan in a single layer; add enough water to cover by at least 1 inch. Bring water to a boil over high heat. Cover and remove from the heat. Let eggs stand in water for 15 minutes. Pour out water. Cool eggs under cold running water. Peel.

Cut eggs in half lengthwise. Remove yolks and transfer to a bowl with jalapeño, habanero, mayonnaise, and mustard. Mash together until smooth. Put yolk mixture in a pastry bag fitted with a decorative tip and squeeze into white halves. Sprinkle with paprika to garnish.

raw_recipe.headline: The Devil's Own Deviled Eggs
raw_recipe.description: The Devil's own deviled egg recipe is a spicy option to the classic. Habanero and jalapeño peppers offer a slow burn that will delight your tastebuds.
raw_recipe.name: The Devil's Own Deviled Eggs

review.reviewBody: I made these for a family gathering a few weeks ago after reading the recipe on here. Everyone loved them. I only used the jalapeno pepper because that is all I had on hand at the time. We had another family gathering a few days ago and I was asked to make them again so this time I used the habanero also and they really liked them. I have a feeling that I will be making these for every family gathering now.

Great change from the ordinary deviled egg recipes out there. Nice kick from the jalapeno and habanero peppers. P.S. I can't stand it when others rate a recipe and they omit a key ingredient and/or change it. Seriously, would you bash a steak recipe if you omitted the steak? Of course it will taste bland if you leave out one of the key ingredients. For those of us who love heat, I'm going to try adding another jalapeno next time just to kick it up a bit more. Thank you for the great recipe Eric.

It was good. I did add a few tweaks to the recipe. I used melted cream cheese, instead of mayo. And I also added 1/8 teaspoon of garlic powder, onion powder and black pepper. Then, also dash of hot sauce and 3 stalks of green onion as garnish. It had a good flavor but it was still a bit dry and bland. Next time, I'm probably gonna try doubling on all the yolk mixture ingredient quantities(except the yolks and peppers), also with my added customizations, plus 1 teaspoon of hot sauce(1 in the yolk mixture, and 1 as garnish on each egg) and 1/2 teaspoon of salt.
Absolutly delicious! Great flavor. I didn't have any haberno peppers, so I used a dash of hot sauce. Came out great anyway.
Love it love it! I added a little more mayo so I could have a softer filling and I didn't use the habanero or paprika and they turned out great! Not too spicy at all.
Will be making this again. I replaced the mayo with greek yogurt (cut down on fat). Absolutely amazing!

I was looking for something different from the 'usual' deviled egg recipe and this is perfect!
Didn't have habaneros, so used all jalapenos and added a little onion when I minced the peppers.
These were for a potluck at work and disappeared within minutes!

Gave this 4 stars because I used the basic premise and veered due to what was in my kitchen. But the concept makes for a really nice deviled egg. I used canned green chilies and a teaspoon of cumin, with a sprinkle of cayenne pepper, and then cayenne pepper instead of paprika, and it was quite delightful.

A favorite when ever the event calls for deviled eggs! I always make some with and without the jalapeños so those who can't take the heat can still enjoy. But the devil's own deviled eggs always go first.
Substituted spicy brown mustard for yellow mustard. Also added a bit of minced olives to be mixed in.

I made it to the recipe except I only had two Jalapeno's. I used the whole peppers and included the seeds and all membranes. I also put a 1/2 slice of peppers on the top. They were a hit at Thanksgiving. I found them to be not as hot I was to be expected so next time I'll try using the Habanero.

Made this for a potluck Cinco de Mayo party - Nothing left over. First time I made it I went a little light on the pepper and dressed it with avocado pieces. The 2nd time made it as the recipe states. It was better, although a bit spicier the 2nd time. This recipe is a winner!
I would add a extra habanero next time to kick up the heat a little bit
Even with the jalapeno and habanero there is very little spice if all seeds are removed. For a kick, leave them in!
This was great, even only having jalapeños on hand.
This was really not that spicy, I was surprised given the title. It was good and they all got eaten but I think it could've used some more heat.

I make these pretty often and they are awesome! Always a big hit at every party! I have noticed that every batch varies in spiciness and that's because of the peppers. Some are just hotter than others I think. When they are too hot, I just add a little bit more mayo to cool them down a bit.

Thanks for the recipe Eric!!
I added some bacon bites for more kick!

Excellent recipe! I went a slightly different approach with a jalapeno and serano pepper, without removing the seeds. Everyone loved the taste and the heat, but definitely give them a heads up that they're spicy. Haha. The first "tester" was taken by surprise. Also, keep an eye on the yolk/mayo ratio. I had to add a little bit of mayo to reach the consistency I wanted, but that could have been my "gestimation" measurements... and not the recipe.
Great recipe! I've made it for my family and multiple parties and it's well-loved. The favorite variation is to add a pickled jalapeno slice on top.
